bug_semantics: Authenticated CRM users with route-level lead permissions could supply another user's lead ID to direct LeadController endpoints. The controller fetched or mutated that ID without checking the lead's user_id against bouncer()->getAuthorizedUserIds(); list and view-permission scoping therefore did not protect the direct edit/update/delete paths, enabling cross-user disclosure, modification, reassignment, and deletion.
flaw_origin: Commit bd24ddb6ebcf4a2d527d71ecb3a4f5d3fea85399 first made the enduring destructive form of the flaw executable: it simultaneously added DELETE leads/{id} -> LeadController@destroy in packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Http/routes.php and added LeadController::destroy() in packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Http/Controllers/Lead/LeadController.php. The new method accepted the caller-controlled ID, checked only that the row existed, and then called $this->leadRepository->delete($id), with no ownership or authorized-user comparison.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object names author Shubham Mehrotra <shubh0896m@gmail.com> and the identical human committer, contains only the subject 'design fixes, lead creation, user account', has no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, no bot identity, and no other AI-attribution marker.
evidence: Advisory sources: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rm5f-3c25-p4cw and https://github.com/TREXNEGRO/Security-Advisories/tree/main/CVE-2026-38530 describe the missing owner check in packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Http/Controllers/Lead/LeadController.php and the crafted GET/PUT/DELETE lead-ID attack. First-party repository issue https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm/issues/2559 independently documents that route ACL middleware does not enforce record ownership, reproduces cross-user edit/updateAttributes/delete, and identifies the same controller; https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm/issues/2462 records the same systemic IDOR. History proof: git log -L over LeadController::destroy and git log -S'$this->leadRepository->delete($id)' both trace the surviving deletion line to https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm/commit/bd24ddb6ebcf4a2d527d71ecb3a4f5d3fea85399. That BIC's diff adds both packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Http/routes.php DELETE '{id}' -> LeadController@destroy and packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Http/Controllers/Lead/LeadController.php destroy(), whose findOrFail($id) is followed by delete($id) without owner authorization. Direct-parent tree checks at 85cf437139289e0cd305c1cfde35d5d3028f556c find neither the destroy method/deletion line nor the DELETE route, proving absence. The BIC is contained by the first release tag v1.0.0 and every later tag. Boundary checks show the unguarded find/delete lines and no preventUnauthorizedAccess call in v2.2.0 (a282e7c3cf969bf10ccc8ebd636be502a58a5a9b), v2.2.1 (a651f7f3a029f16ccbb2e6461f4c4f64badfb04e), v2.2.2 (e0670bb8f0c0bb72aab430d070eb86bd8114ff71), and v2.2.3 (6cda4f6297042d74769c38fcbc1b7ebe6df54ab6); thus the advisory's published '<= 2.2.0' range understates the source-visible affected boundary. Direct fix https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm/commit/cccc12df2c405f6c00633bff13d7befd8dd0ee4f adds Controller::preventUnauthorizedAccess()/filterAuthorizedRecords() and applies the ownership check before LeadController edit, update, updateAttributes, updateStage, destroy, massUpdate, and massDestroy. First-party PR https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm/pull/2567 lands that direct fix through merge https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm/commit/e1eb78586fc1bba0204de12222a7f10b53986cc9. Both the merge and direct fix are contained by v2.2.4 (55b48fe86d7f196c32581ed80bb723cf0e18d44e), whose controller contains the guards, making v2.2.4 the first source-proven patched tag; the advisory itself supplies no first_patched_version.
reasoning: The causal unit is not a later refactor or the broad 2026 fix: bd24ddb6ebcf4a2d527d71ecb3a4f5d3fea85399 is the smallest ordinary one-parent commit that first wired an attacker-reachable lead deletion endpoint and wrote its unscoped repository deletion. Its direct parent lacks both route and method, while git -L/-S show the deletion survived subsequent formatting/refactors into the advisory-tested 2.2.x code. Later ownership-aware listing/view logic made the authorization asymmetry explicit, but did not originate the enduring deletion line. The flaw remained in tagged releases through v2.2.3. Direct commit cccc12df2c405f6c00633bff13d7befd8dd0ee4f fixes the mechanism by checking the record owner against the authorized-user set before direct operations, and merge e1eb78586fc1bba0204de12222a7f10b53986cc9 lands PR #2567 before v2.2.4. AI attribution is judged only from the BIC object; its human author/committer and trailer-free message contain no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
